title: plugin-audit: a user's own sys_user_preference writes (ui.recent) come back to them as "Updated User Preference 'ui.recent'" inbox notifications — the console bell shows six of them and nothing else
body:
Item 5 of objectstack-ai/cloud#2772. Filed from the cloud maintainer's session with the maintainer's agreement on 2026-10-12 (「同意」). ⛔ Not a claim.

## Source

2026-10-12 staging walk-through of the cloud console: `cloud.objectos.app`, org 「2531 hotcrm 验收」, owner account; cloud `63ea887f`, objectui pin `d758f2f2`, framework pin as cloud `.objectstack-sha` at that commit.

## What the user sees

Cloud console, bell icon → 消息中心: six entries 「Updated User Preference 'ui.recent'」, subtitle 「系统通知 · sys_user_preference」, and nothing else. They are the audit trail of the console's own "Recently accessed" writes (objectui#11678 made that write happen only when the list changes, so each navigation that changes the list still writes once). A new user opens the bell and reads six machine messages about a table they have never heard of.

![notification center](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/cloud/blob/fdd422db1e94a4190958fb770bd21ad1ae520e63/12-notification-center.jpg?raw=true)

## Mechanism (to confirm)

`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts` emits the L2 event and the inbox fan-out through the ADR-0030 single ingress for audited writes. Its `SKIP_OBJECTS` list (`audit-writers.ts:166` onward) excludes sessions, jobs, notifications and the inbox itself, but not `sys_user_preference`, so a user's own UI-state write comes back to them as a system notification. Precedent: objectstack#3402 (file-assignment noise notifications).

## Fix direction (recommended)

1. Add `sys_user_preference` (and any other per-user UI-state table) to `SKIP_OBJECTS`, or stop the inbox fan-out for self-authored writes on system tables; keep the audit log row if auditing needs it.
2. Write the rule down next to the list: a notification is for something another actor did or something that needs the user; the user's own UI-state writes never qualify.

## Acceptance

1. Fresh user, navigate five console pages, open the bell: zero `sys_user_preference` entries.
2. The audit log still records the write if `sys_user_preference` stays audited, or the card states it is excluded.
3. Unit test on the writer: a write to `sys_user_preference` produces no `sys_inbox_message`.

## Related

objectstack#3402 · objectui#11678 · ADR-0030
